beats.text: In 1940 ordinary wind tore a new bridge apart.
It bounced in plain wind and was called Galloping Gertie.
Its road was a solid slab, so wind hit it like a sail.
Wind tilts the road, and a tilted road catches more.
Not just wind. The tilt made the wind push harder.
An hour later, it broke apart.
Now engineers blow wind on tiny models.
The new bridge has gaps, so wind slips through.
Follow for more, and see how everything works.
